prompt: How many angles $\theta$ between $0^\circ$ and $360^\circ$ make $\sin\theta = 0.5$ true?
hint: $\sin\theta$ is the HEIGHT of the point. Draw a flat line at height $0.5$ across the unit circle and count the crossings.

hints.text: $\sin\theta$ is the HEIGHT of the point. Draw a flat line at height $0.5$ across the unit circle and count the crossings.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try height $0$ first: the circle sits at height $0$ at $0^\circ$ and again at $180^\circ$ — two spots in one turn. A flat line usually cuts a circle in two places. Now do the same at height $0.5$.
The line at height $0.5$ cuts the circle once on the way up (Quadrant 1) and once on the way back down (Quadrant 2).

explanation: Picture the unit circle and a flat horizontal line drawn at height $0.5$.
Going once around, you pass through that height on the way UP at $30^\circ$ and again on the way DOWN at $150^\circ$.
So there are $2$ solutions in one full turn. Almost every basic trig equation has TWO answers per turn.

alternativeExplanations.title: Read it off the wave graph
steps: Graph y = sin θ from 0° to 360° — it rises to 1, falls to −1, and comes back.
Draw the flat line y = 0.5 across it. The wave crosses that line twice: once climbing, once falling.

alternativeExplanations.title: Think of a rotating platform
steps: A seat on a spinning platform passes each height twice per turn — once rising, once falling.
The only heights hit just once are the very top and the very bottom. 0.5 is neither, so it gets hit twice.
